items.statement: The submitted first-event TS is characterized by a reaction-relevant imaginary mode and a path calculation connects it to the stated reactant-side and product-side states.
items.expected: Frequency and IRC/equivalent path evidence are reported for the selected candidate, with the reactant and product-side identities explicit.

items.statement: The investigation tests the authors' qualitative two-step substitution hypothesis and records candidate generation/deduplication and rejection evidence.
items.expected: The report explicitly maps its candidate/path analysis to a two-step six-membered-ring hypothesis without asserting a paper numerical answer as an input.

items.statement: The first substitution barrier is the source-backed quantitative endpoint.
items.expected: A completed report gives a first-event free-energy barrier near the published 152.4 kJ mol-1 under its stated model/reference, or a bounded failure transparently explains why no defensible value was obtained.

items.statement: The first acylation belongs to the rate-limiting portion of C3O2 generation in the authors' interpretation.
items.expected: The conclusion discusses whether the independently computed first event supports the qualitative rate-determining interpretation, while separating source comparison from proof of experimental kinetics.
